Bergen County Courthouse

The Bergen County Courthouse, also known as the Bergen Justice Center, is a cornerstone of legal and historical significance in Hackensack, New Jersey. Designed by the renowned architect James Riely Gordon, it serves not only as a functional judicial hub but also as an iconic landmark with rich historical relevance. This guide provides an in-depth overview of the courthouse’s history, services, and practical information for visitors and residents.

History of Bergen County Courthouse

The Bergen County Courthouse, established in the early 20th century, is an architectural masterpiece. Constructed under the direction of James Riely Gordon, it boasts a neoclassical design featuring grand columns, intricate carvings, and durable materials. Over the years, the courthouse has been the site of many landmark cases and community events, cementing its role as a historical and judicial epicenter.

Key Services Offered at Bergen County Courthouse

The Bergen County Courthouse provides a wide range of services to address civil, criminal, traffic, and family law matters. Key departments include:

  • Clerk’s Office: Handles public records, marriage licenses, and passport applications.
  • Judicial Divisions: Dedicated to civil, criminal, probate, and family law cases.
  • Mediation Services: Offers peaceful resolution options for family and divorce-related disputes.

Architectural and Design Details

The courthouse’s design is a testament to classic architectural principles. Highlights include:

  • Neoclassical façade with towering columns.
  • 240,000 square feet of interconnected courtrooms and agency spaces.
  • Durable construction materials chosen for longevity and aesthetic appeal.

How to Access Bergen County Courthouse

Address

10 Main Street, Hackensack, NJ 07601

Parking

Public parking is conveniently located at 55 Court Street, adjacent to the courthouse.

Public Transportation

Accessible via local bus and train services, ensuring ease of access for visitors.

FAQs About Bergen County Courthouse

What are the operational hours?

  • Monday to Friday: 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM
  • Saturday and Sunday: Closed

How do I contact the Clerk’s Office?

  • Phone: 201-336-7000
  • Email: countyclerk@co.bergen.nj.us

Where is the passport counter located?

The passport counter is in the Clerk’s Office at One Bergen County Plaza, Room 120, Hackensack, NJ.

Local and Legal Significance

The courthouse is integral to the Bergen County community, handling high-profile cases and contributing to the region’s legal framework. It is also a cultural landmark, reflecting the area’s historical evolution.

Nearby Attractions and Services

Visitors can explore nearby historical sites, parks, and restaurants, making a trip to the courthouse both practical and enjoyable. Popular options include:

  • Bergen County Historical Museum
  • Cafés and dining options in downtown Hackensack
  • Local parks and recreational facilities

For more details about the Bergen County Courthouse’s services, history, and updates, visit Bergen County Official Website or contact their helpline at 201-527-2700. Whether you’re looking to resolve legal matters, explore historical architecture, or simply learn more, the Bergen County Courthouse is ready to assist.
